newsitem.title: USA: Farmland combines meat and livestock businesses.
newsitem.headline: Farmland combines meat and livestock businesses.

text.p: Farmland Industries Inc said it had restructured its livestock, meat and food groups into a single business unit to create a "farm to table" production and marketing chain.

"The Farmland Meats Group will function as a world-class food chain, stretching from optimized livestock production to efficient manufacturing of value-added brand marketing for the consumer," said Farmland chief executive Harry Cleberg.
The Meats Group will include Farmland Foods, Livestock Production, and Farmland's Beef and Pork processing units and be headed by Gary Evans, Farmland executive vice president.
Farmland is the largest farmer-owned cooperative in North America, with 1996 sales of $9.8 billion that included $3.2 billion in meat products and $3.5 billion in grain.

"Producers must gear up to be more competitive in the global marketplace. To do so, they must adopt new technology, reduce costs, replace herds with superior breeding stock, develop seamless or integrated systems, and form alliances and new generation cooperatives," Evans said.

"Our producers know what is expected of them. They know they are no longer raising cattle and hogs. Instead, they're producing beef and pork products. They're not in this business to please packing plants but to satisfy food consumers," he said.
Farmland sold food products in 74 countries last year.
